summary: Alert webhook payload cutoff dropping tracehook parameters for long embedding/route tokens
description:
Issue summary: Customers (FinTrove) report that alert webhook payloads sent from Console occasionally arrive at their downstream automation with the tracehook parameters missing or truncated. The tracehook parameter contains a route token and trace_id that downstream systems use to correlate alerts with traces. When truncated, the customer's automated triage removes the link to the trace and human investigation becomes manual.

Impact: Enterprise customer FinTrove experiences loss of trace links for a subset (~6-7%) of alerts during high-cardinality alerting windows. This increases MTTR since on-call must manually search traces. The problem appears intermittent and correlates with alerts that include long route tokens or extra context in the alert payload.

Observed behavior: Console sends webhook POSTs where the body is truncated at ~8192 bytes (observed) and the "tracehook" parameter is partially or completely missing on the receiving side (customer webhook endpoint logs). Alerts otherwise show as delivered (no retry).

Expected behavior: Webhook POSTs should include the full JSON payload or form payload including tracehook params so downstream automation receives trace links reliably.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a console alert that includes expanded context and uses a route_token that is ~2.5k chars (simulated long base64 token).
2) Configure webhook notification to point at a test endpoint that logs raw request bodies (customer provided curl server).
3) Trigger alert by firing synthetic events that match the alert rule, ensuring payload size will exceed 8kb after url-encoding metadata fields.
4) Observe test endpoint logs and compare to the payload shown in Console 'Delivered' audit trail.
logs: edge-proxy (us-east-1) request_id=abc123 - upstream POST to customer webhook started: 2026-03-10T16:12:02Z
console-webhook-dispatcher dispatcher_id=wd-77 - payload_length=8144 bytes before encoding, encoded_length=10238 bytes
customer-endpoint logs - received body length: 8192, tracehook param truncated after 3k chars
nginx error: client intended to send too large body: 8192 bytes (observed on staging repro proxy)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: encoding/transfer mechanism used by Console webhook sender switches to application/x-www-form-urlencoded for legacy alerts and percent-encoding expands token size causing upstream proxy to drop/truncate body.

Reproduced in staging by sending alert with long token - observed truncation at ~8192 bytes in test endpoint captured with tcpdump and confirmed by comparing with dispatcher payload copy stored in S3 (partial).

Edge NGINX config uses default large_client_header_buffers and client_body_buffer_size that result in rejection/truncation for large encoded form payloads when combined with long headers and query params.
Console audit shows 'Delivered' status because the webhook sender received a 200 from the proxy before the proxy forwarded truncated body to the customer endpoint (proxy returned success on chunk 1).
Workaround confirmed: switching webhook to application/json POST (not form-encoded) preserves tracehook field and avoids truncation in our staging repro.
Risk: several customers and internal default alert templates still use the legacy form-encoded path for webhooks; rollout must not break smaller payloads and must preserve backward compatibility.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported 17 alerts overnight with missing trace links. Provided request captures and suggested temporary change to JSON webhooks but customer asked for a more permanent fix.
Rafael Ortega (SRE) 2026-03-11: Confirmed repro in staging. Suspect nginx buffer limit + percent-encoding expansion. Filed infra task to validate nginx buffers in edge-proxy clusters.
Elena Park (Customer Success) 2026-03-11: Escalated to account exec. Customer requests ETA for fix; prioritized due to enterprise SLAs.

Rafael Ortega (SRE) 2026-03-12: Created PR to switch console webhook sender to always POST application/json and use chunked transfer-encoding for large payloads. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4826. Running canary in staging 2/3 nodes.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer: update notification endpoint configuration to 'POST JSON' in Console (Settings > Alerts > Notification Methods) as interim. Documented steps and sample payload provided.
Short-term fix: update edge-proxy nginx config to increase client_body_buffer_size and large_client_header_buffers in us-east-1 to handle encoded payloads during migration window.
Long-term fix: switch webhook sender to application/json + chunked transfer to avoid url-encoding expansion. PR created and under review (see related_github_prs).
Follow-up: add automated e2e test covering large alert payloads and add telemetry to track webhook payload size and downstream truncation events.
